knowledge_graph.title: Ketogenic diet
knowledge_graph.description: The ketogenic diet is a high-fat, adequate-protein, low-carbohydrate dietary therapy that in conventional medicine is used mainly to treat hard-to-control epilepsy in children. The diet forces the body to burn fats rather than carbohydrates.

related_questions.question: What foods are on a keto diet?

text_blocks.snippet: A keto diet primarily consists of high-fat foods, moderate protein, and very low carbohydrates. Key foods include meats, fish, eggs, cheese, nuts, seeds, and certain low-carbohydrate vegetables. Fruits, grains, and starchy vegetables are generally avoided.
snippet_highlighted_words: meats, fish, eggs, cheese, nuts, seeds, and certain low-carbohydrate vegetables

list.snippet: Meat and Poultry: Beef, chicken, turkey, and other meats are keto-friendly, especially those with higher fat content.
Fish and Seafood: Fatty fish like salmon, tuna, and mackerel, as well as shrimp, lobster, and other seafood, are good choices according to CookUnity and ZOE.
Eggs: A versatile and keto staple, eggs are high in protein and healthy fats.
Cheese: Unprocessed cheeses like cheddar, mozzarella, and goat cheese are good options according to Quora and Banner Health.
Nuts and Seeds: Almonds, walnuts, chia seeds, flax seeds, and others are keto-friendly.
Avocado: A great source of healthy fats and nutrients.
Healthy Oils: Olive oil, coconut oil, and others are important for adding fat.
Low-Carbohydrate Vegetables: Leafy greens like spinach and kale, broccoli, cauliflower, and zucchini are good choices.
Berries: Small amounts of berries like blueberries and raspberries can be included, as they are lower in carbs than other fruits according to University of California - Davis Health and EatingWell.
Grains: Rice, pasta, bread, and other grains are high in carbohydrates.
Starchy Vegetables: Potatoes, corn, peas, and other starchy vegetables are generally avoided.
Sugary Fruits: Most fruits are high in carbohydrates and should be limited.
Sugary Drinks: Sodas, juices, and sweetened beverages are not keto-friendly.
Processed Foods: Many processed foods are high in carbohydrates and unhealthy fats.
Legumes: Beans, lentils, and other legumes are typically avoided.

text_blocks.snippet: The ketogenic diet's healthfulness is debated. While it can be beneficial for certain conditions, like epilepsy in children, and may aid in weight loss, it also carries potential risks like nutrient deficiencies, heart health issues, and gastrointestinal problems. The diet's strict nature makes it challenging to maintain long-term and may not be suitable for everyone, especially those with pre-existing health conditions.
snippet_highlighted_words: The ketogenic diet's healthfulness is debated

list.title: Weight Loss:
list.snippet: The keto diet can promote weight loss by reducing appetite and increasing fat burning.

list.title: Improved Blood Sugar Control:
list.snippet: Some studies suggest that the keto diet may help manage blood sugar levels in people with type 2 diabetes.

list.title: Epilepsy Management:
list.snippet: The keto diet has been used as a therapeutic approach for managing epilepsy, particularly in children.

list.title: Potential Neuroprotective Effects:
list.snippet: Some research indicates that ketones produced during ketosis may have neuroprotective properties.

list.title: Nutrient Deficiencies:
list.snippet: The restrictive nature of the keto diet can lead to deficiencies in vitamins and minerals due to the limited intake of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.

list.title: Heart Health Concerns:
list.snippet: High intake of saturated fats, common in the keto diet, can negatively impact cholesterol levels and potentially increase the risk of heart disease.

list.title: Gastrointestinal Issues:
list.snippet: Low fiber intake on the keto diet can cause constipation and other digestive problems.

list.title: "Keto Flu":
list.snippet: The initial transition to ketosis can cause flu-like symptoms like fatigue, nausea, and headaches.

list.title: Potential for Disordered Eating:
list.snippet: The strict nature of the diet may trigger or exacerbate disordered eating patterns in some individuals.

list.title: Long-term Sustainability:
list.snippet: The restrictive nature of the keto diet makes it difficult to maintain long-term for many individuals.

list.title: Individual Health Conditions:
list.snippet: The keto diet is not recommended for individuals with pancreatic, liver, thyroid, or gallbladder issues.

list.title: Individual Needs:
list.snippet: The potential benefits and risks of the keto diet can vary depending on individual health goals and dietary preferences.

list.title: Dietary Choices:
list.snippet: The specific foods chosen within the keto diet can significantly impact its effects on heart health and overall well-being.

list.title: Professional Guidance:
list.snippet: Consulting with a healthcare professional or registered dietitian is recommended before starting the keto diet, especially if you have any pre-existing health conditions or concerns, according to Endeavor Health.

related_questions.question: What is the difference between a keto diet and a ketogenic diet?
related_questions.snippet: They are sometimes referred to as ketogenic or "keto" diets. But a true ketogenic diet is different. Unlike other low-carb diets, which focus on protein, a keto plan centers on fat, which supplies as much as 90% of daily calories. And it's not the type of diet to try as an experiment.
related_questions.title: Should you try the keto diet? - Harvard Health

text_blocks.snippet: The ketogenic (keto) diet is a high-fat, very low-carbohydrate, and moderate-protein eating plan that causes the body to produce ketones as an alternative fuel source instead of glucose. This metabolic state, called ketosis, can be beneficial for weight loss, blood sugar management, and potentially other health conditions.
snippet_highlighted_words: a high-fat, very low-carbohydrate, and moderate-protein eating plan that causes the body to produce ketones as an alternative fuel source instead of glucose

list.title: Low Carbohydrates:
list.snippet: The keto diet drastically reduces carbohydrate intake, typically to 20-50 grams per day.

list.title: High Fat:
list.snippet: Fat becomes the primary source of calories, usually making up 70-80% of the diet.

list.title: Moderate Protein:
list.snippet: Protein intake is moderate, providing a source of amino acids for bodily functions.

list.title: Ketosis:
list.snippet: When carbohydrate intake is severely limited, the body begins to break down fat into ketones in the liver.

list.title: Energy Source:
list.snippet: These ketones are then used as an alternative fuel source for the body and brain.

list.title: Benefits:
list.snippet: Keto diets are often associated with weight loss, improved blood sugar control, and may have other potential benefits, though more research is needed.

list.title: Medical Use:
list.snippet: The keto diet has been used for decades to treat epilepsy, especially in children who don't respond to medication.
